comparator.name: English Language and Culture
comparator.sourceNotes: The 180 EC English Linguistics and Literature example follows the full-time programme. It has a common first year, selected linguistics core options and 12 EC of programme-related electives in year two, and a research seminar and 12 EC thesis in year three.
components: English Literature 1: Genres, Texts and Contexts
English Linguistics 4: Research in English Linguistics
English Literature 5: Modern and Contemporary Literature
English Linguistics 6: The Changing English Language
Philosophy of the Humanities (LCA and English)
Bachelor's Thesis English Language and Culture

courses: New Issues in Contemporary Social Theory

core: English-language literature across periods, cultures and forms
English language, its structures, histories and global varieties
The relationship between language, literature, culture, history and identity
Close reading, rhetoric, academic writing, literary theory and textual research
Sociolinguistics, World Englishes and language change across societies
Humanities research methods, research seminar and independent bachelor research
adjacent: English in media, politics, science and public communication
Postcolonial literature, empire, race, gender and class
questions: How do English-language texts represent identity, power and social change?
How has English changed and diversified across historical and global communities?

routeSelection.basis: The normalized target names the general English Language and Culture bachelor rather than one specialisation. Of the two official specialisations, English Linguistics and Literature most broadly preserves the programme title’s combined language-and-literature identity, while World Literatures in English is the more specialised literature route. The combined route is selected independently of UCR fit.

selection.assessment: Three coherent options reach the maximum. They prioritise combined literary and language study, world literatures and adaptation, or language and public culture. The options differ by 52.5, 45 and 67.5 EC each way.

alternatives.label: Literature, Language and Culture
alternatives.labelReason: Introductory literature, rhetoric and brain and behaviour support stylistics, psycholinguistics, literary theory and evidence synthesis.
alternatives.concept: Study literary works and the ways language creates meaning. Combine close reading, stylistics and psycholinguistics with cultural history, media and research methods.
progression: Introductory literature, rhetoric and brain and behaviour support stylistics, psycholinguistics, literary theory and evidence synthesis.

alternatives.label: World Literatures and Adaptation
alternatives.labelReason: Literary and film foundations precede adaptation, documentary production and advanced interpretation. Historical and visual study help situate texts and their reception.
alternatives.concept: Study how stories change as they move between cultures and media. Combine world literature, myth, literary theory and film adaptation with study of empire, visual culture and documentary.
alternatives.distinctness: Myth, adaptation, documentary and visual-cultural interpretation shape the selection.
progression: Literary and film foundations precede adaptation, documentary production and advanced interpretation. Historical and visual study help situate texts and their reception.

alternatives.label: Language, Identity and Public Culture
alternatives.labelReason: Brain and behaviour precedes psycholinguistics and higher cognition. Sociology and rhetoric precede qualitative research, public persuasion and media analysis.
alternatives.concept: Study how language and media shape identity and public life. Combine stylistics, rhetoric and psycholinguistics with social theory, cultural history and research on representation.
alternatives.distinctness: Language, cognition, social institutions, identity and public persuasion shape the selection.
progression: Brain and behaviour precedes psycholinguistics and higher cognition. Sociology and rhetoric precede qualitative research, public persuasion and media analysis.

blocks: Both teach close reading and critical interpretation across literary genres.
Both examine literary texts in historical context. UCR reads across a wider range of periods and traditions.
Both develop close interpretation and a research-based argument. UCR focuses on life and travel writing.
Both apply critical theories to literary interpretation.
UvA studies eighteenth-century English writing as a distinct period.
UvA studies nineteenth-century literature as a distinct period.
UvA studies modern and contemporary literature in a separate course.
UvA requires a second course in close textual research.
Both analyse rhetoric and develop arguments for particular audiences. UvA gives dedicated attention to academic writing.
Both analyse how language creates meaning in context. UCR focuses on stylistics, while UvA teaches English syntax in greater depth.
UvA studies the social history of English and the structure of words.
UvA studies the spread of English and how it varies around the world.
UvA teaches methods for collecting and analysing language data. UCR offers general research methods.
This example studies how English varies across communities and social settings.
This example studies how English changes over time. UCR’s Psycholinguistics course studies how people process and acquire language.
Students choose 12 EC from approved English Language and Culture options.
Students have 12 EC of free electives in year two.
UvA examines how researchers produce knowledge in the humanities.
UvA examines current debates in English linguistics and literary studies.
The research seminar develops the topic and methods for the thesis.
Students have 30 EC of free electives in year three.
UvA requires a thesis after the research seminar. UCR independent research is optional.

notes.text: UvA has dedicated courses in English grammar, language history, varieties of English and literary periods. UCR offers related study in literature, stylistics, language processing and culture.

audience.programmeDescription: English Language and Culture at the University of Amsterdam studies English-language literature and the history, structure and use of English. This example follows English Linguistics and Literature.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The closest UCR option combines literary and language study. Other options focus on world literatures and adaptation or on language and public culture. UvA offers dedicated sequences in English linguistics and literary history and requires a thesis.

curriculum.limitation: The literacy diagnostic and study tutoring carry no credits.
